name: Vision
description: Whether the government has a clear vision for implementing artificial intelligence. Captures the existence of an overarching, publicly available national AI strategy that articulates the government's high-level policy vision for how AI will be developed and used to benefit the country.

name: Governance and Ethics
description: Whether the right regulations and ethical frameworks are in place to implement AI in a way that builds trust and legitimacy. Covers data protection and privacy legislation, cybersecurity, the legal framework's adaptability to digital business models, a national AI ethics framework, and public-sector accountability.

name: Digital Capacity
description: The existing digital capacity within government. Covers the maturity of online public services and e-government delivery, foundational government IT infrastructure, and government promotion of investment in emerging technologies.

name: Adaptability
description: Whether the government can change and innovate effectively. Covers overall government effectiveness, the government's responsiveness to change, and the use of open data in public procurement.

name: Maturity
description: Whether the country has a technology sector capable of supplying government with AI technologies. Covers the number of AI and non-AI technology unicorns, the value of trade in ICT services and goods per capita, and computer software spending. (Labelled 'Size' in the 2021 edition.)

name: Innovation Capacity
description: Whether the technology sector has the right conditions to support innovation. Covers the ease of business administrative requirements, venture-capital availability, research and development spending, company investment in emerging technology, and AI research-paper output.

name: Human Capital
description: Whether the population has the right skills to support the technology sector. Covers STEM graduates, software-developer (GitHub) activity, female STEM graduates, the quality of engineering and technology higher education, and general digital skills.

name: Infrastructure
description: Whether the country has good technological infrastructure to support AI technologies. Covers telecommunications infrastructure, availability of cloud-provider regions, broadband quality, 5G infrastructure, and adoption of emerging technologies.

name: Data Availability
description: Whether there is good, representative availability of data that could be used to train AI models. Covers open data, data governance, mobile-cellular subscriptions, household internet access and statistical capacity, together with equity of access including the internet gender gap and the affordability of internet-enabled devices.

name: Data Representativeness
description: Whether the available data is likely to be representative of the population as a whole. Covers the internet-access gender gap and the cost of an internet-enabled device relative to GDP per capita.

Policy Capacity
description: The extent to which the government can design and implement effective AI policies aligned with a clear, national policy vision for how AI benefits the country, demonstrating commitment by assigning resources to that vision and engaging in international cooperation to address AI's global nature.
source: Oxford Insights GAIRI 2025 Methodology Report, p.6

name: Governance
description: The extent to which the government has clear governance principles that shape how AI is developed and adopted while protecting people's rights and societal interests, promoted through its own public-sector practices and ensuring an adaptive environment for regulatory compliance with respect to AI.
source: Oxford Insights GAIRI 2025 Methodology Report, p.6

name: AI Infrastructure
description: The extent to which there is adequate compute capacity and enabling technical infrastructure that government and other actors can rely on over the long term to develop and use AI, with sufficient high-quality data that is accessible and flows securely within and across borders.
source: Oxford Insights GAIRI 2025 Methodology Report, p.6

name: Public Sector Adoption
description: The extent to which the government's digital policy encourages testing how AI can solve public-sector challenges and, where AI proves effective, scales those solutions, demonstrated through its e-government delivery capabilities.
source: Oxford Insights GAIRI 2025 Methodology Report, p.6

name: Development & Diffusion
description: The extent to which there is a mature AI sector able to meet the needs of local clients and consumers and push long-term AI innovation, backed by sufficient human capital to meet demand for wider AI technology diffusion among industry, researchers and civil society.
source: Oxford Insights GAIRI 2025 Methodology Report, p.6

name: Resilience
description: The extent to which the government manages the social, economic and environmental challenges of a societal transition towards widespread AI adoption, actively monitoring and preparing for new risks to national safety and security as AI development and diffusion progresses.
source: Oxford Insights GAIRI 2025 Methodology Report, p.6

name: Policy vision
description: Whether the government has published a clear national AI strategy and high-level vision, including an AI advisory council and stated intent to participate in international cooperation on AI research and governance.

name: Policy commitment
description: Whether the strategy is backed by implementation: published actions, outputs and a timeline (a roadmap with designated ministries and monitoring methods), and updates to policy over time.

name: Compute capacity
description: Whether the country has adequate computational resources (for example data-centre and processing capacity) that government and other actors can rely on to develop and use AI.

name: Enabling technical infrastructure
description: Whether foundational connectivity and technical infrastructure (networks, broadband, cloud) are in place to support AI development and deployment.

name: Data quality
description: Whether sufficient, high-quality data is available and accessible for a wide range of AI problems, flowing securely within and across borders.

name: Governance principles
description: Whether the government promotes clear principles for the responsible development and adoption of AI that protect people's rights and societal interests.

name: Regulatory compliance
description: Whether an adaptive regulatory environment supports and enforces compliance for the development and use of AI.

name: Government digital policy
description: Whether government digital policy encourages testing and piloting of AI to solve public-sector challenges.

name: e-Government delivery
description: Whether the government scales effective AI solutions, demonstrated through the maturity of its digital and e-government service delivery.

name: Human capital
description: Whether there is sufficient human capital and skills to support a domestic AI sector and wider adoption of AI.

name: AI sector maturity
description: Whether there is a mature domestic AI sector able to meet the needs of local clients and drive long-term AI innovation.

name: AI technology diffusion
description: Whether AI technologies are diffusing among industry players, researchers and civil society who apply AI in their domains.

name: Societal transition
description: Whether the government manages the social, economic and environmental challenges of a societal transition towards widespread AI adoption.

name: Safety and security
description: Whether the government actively monitors and prepares for new risks to national safety and security as AI develops and diffuses.

name: National AI Strategy
description: Evidence of an overarching published national AI strategy demonstrating a whole-of-government policy vision (100 published / 50 draft or announced / 0 none).

name: AI Advisory Council
description: A multistakeholder body of AI experts advising government on AI implementation and use, broader in remit than drafting the strategy itself.

name: Publication of Strategy Updates
description: Whether the country has published policy documentation beyond its original strategy (additional phase, implementation plan or further strategy).

name: International Cooperation on AI R&D
description: Active joint R&D collaborations, bilateral agreements, co-funded initiatives or hosting of major international AI R&D events.

name: International Cooperation on AI Governance
description: Engaged participation in global AI governance fora and contribution to international AI safety or governance standards.

indicator: Actions, outputs and timeline in AI Strategy
name: Actions, outputs and timeline in AI Strategy
description: Whether the strategy includes a robust implementation roadmap: specific actions, designated ministries, a timeline and monitoring methods (100 roadmap / 50 actions only / 0 none).
